supporting_observations.claim: The alerted PowerShell activity is visible: at 13:44:39 UTC, powershell.exe ran on WS-MLOPEZ-01 as HARBOR-DENTAL\omar.haddad with the command line referencing \\FILE-HD-01\IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1.
Shortly before PowerShell started, WS-MLOPEZ-01 recorded a network logon for omar.haddad from WS-OHADDAD-01; the logon was granted the listed privileges.
The observed account, patch script path, and timing match the environment's stated practice of omar.haddad running that script remotely, and its scheduled business-hours workstation patching.

The process and network evidence provides a specific benign explanation for the PowerShell activity: it launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update package, and the same window includes a Windows Update download through the proxy.
Process termination records show both the update installer and the PowerShell process exited shortly afterward.

known_telemetry_limitations: The evidence records the PowerShell command line and its child process, but does not include the contents of Deploy-Patches.ps1.
The logs establish that PowerShell ran, but do not establish whether a visible PowerShell window appeared on Maria Lopez's desktop.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not independently verify the contents or integrity of the patch script or the update package.
The evidence does not establish that Maria Lopez saw the PowerShell window or identify the exact time she noticed it.
unrelated_findings: A svc-bkp credential-use event on WS-MLOPEZ-01 targeted PROXY-HD-01. The inventory places svc-bkp on FILE-HD-01; this is outside the alerted PowerShell activity and merits separate review. (T024-00043)
GlobalProtect PanGPS.exe ran on WS-MLOPEZ-01, although the environment inventory says there is no VPN. This record alone does not establish that a VPN connection occurred. (T024-00039, T024-00040)
Google Drive File Stream started on WS-MLOPEZ-01; the inventory approves OneDrive but no other cloud-storage services. (T024-00278, T024-00280)
